zh.summary: Energy mechanisms, formulas, dates, medium-specific Cherenkov condition and source attribution are sound. Restore the explicit direction of the historical consumption ratio and declare the historical institution individually.

en.summary: Scientific meaning and the historical qualifiers are retained without new physical or historical facts. The institution declaration and complete-sentence short-paragraph layout need targeted revision.

findings.title: Make the numerator and denominator of the historical lamp-consumption ratio explicit
findings.sourceMeaning: The ordinary incandescent lamp's electricity consumption is approximately 1.5 to 2 times the fluorescent lamp's electricity consumption.
findings.candidateMeaning: The Chinese text gives a consumption comparison between the two lamps as one and a half to two times, but does not say which lamp consumes that multiple of the other.
findings.impact: A learner cannot determine the direction of the quantitative statement from the Chinese sentence itself. The numerical endpoints survive, but the source's directional relation does not; the English candidate more clearly associates the larger consumption with the incandescent lamp.
findings.requiredRevision: State explicitly that the incandescent lamp's consumption is approximately 1.5 to 2 times the fluorescent lamp's, keeping the existing attribution to the textbook's lamps and technological conditions. Do not add an equal-light-output condition, a modern efficiency value, or a new experimental premise.

findings.title: Declare the historical Academy of Sciences separately from the country
findings.observation: The institution and the 1945 to 1951 presidency remain in both texts, but neither historical_entities array declares the institution. Existing entries declare the country/demonym and people; the country substring is not an individual declaration of the institution.
findings.contract: .claude/skills/ld-s10y-lesson/SKILL.md cap4 item 3 requires individual source-bound declarations for real scientific-history people, places, countries and institutions.
findings.requiredRevision: Add an institution-specific declaration in each locale with the exact candidate term, the original institution as source_term where appropriate, and a reason bound to this block's history. Keep the English translation declaration. Do not change the institution's identity or dates, or resolve the source's other name-initial uncertainties by invention.

findings.title: Keep full sentences within short English paragraphs

exactBoundary.before: Accelerating charged particles can emit electromagnetic waves;
exactBoundary.after: such particles are present in the atoms that make up matter.

findings.observation: The existing text-only prose_flow.mjs output confirms that /prose/1 contains a blank-line paragraph break inside this semicolon-linked sentence. The next paragraph begins with lowercase 'such' and also contains five full sentences. Other unsplit English paragraphs contain four sentences at /prose/3, /prose/5 and /prose/15, six at /prose/6, and five at /prose/11.
findings.impact: The charged-particle explanation is broken across independently displayed paragraphs, and the long biography and multi-example paragraphs exceed the prescribed two-to-three-sentence reading units. Single line breaks do not fix this: htmlfrag.js proseParagraphs splits at blank lines.
findings.requiredRevision: Keep the charged-particle sentence together and divide these English passages at complete-sentence boundaries into coherent two-to-three-sentence paragraphs, with complete sentences on their own lines. Preserve every source-bound block and its refs, all existing scientific qualifications and the empty portrait block. This is candidate text/layout revision only; it does not authorize native finalization or DISPLAY approval.

sourceBoundObservations.observation: Both introduce the change from light propagation to light production. The added distinction explains the source transition rather than adding a new physical claim or filler.

Both retain the approximate historical visible-light range as $4\times10^{-5}$ to $8\times10^{-5}$ centimeters, with the negative exponents, endpoints and unit unchanged. Both retain accelerated charges, atomic structure, the piano-string analogy, excitation by supplied energy and subsequent emission; 'can' avoids implying that every excitation must emit light. English meaning is equivalent, but its charged-particle sentence crosses a blank-line boundary.

Both preserve the central energy accounting: energy must be supplied before atomic emission, emission uses acquired energy, and sustained emission needs a continuing external supply. Neither portrays light as a pre-existing substance stored inside an atom.

The source's thermal-motion and collision explanation is explicitly a simplified textbook atomic model in both locales. Increasing temperature, more vigorous thermal motion and partial kinetic-energy conversion to excitation are preserved, without upgrading this model to an exhaustive theory of thermal radiation. English puts all four sentences into one paragraph.

Both retain the Sun, hot incandescent filament and burning-fuel soot as thermal-emission examples. The 3 to 4% figure is attributed to the textbook and remains the fraction of current-supplied filament energy converted to light, not a total-radiation efficiency or a universal present-day lamp specification. Wood, kerosene, gas and incompletely burned particles remain; no added equal-output comparison or altered number appears.

Both retain the gas-discharge sequence: the electric field supplies electron kinetic energy, fast electrons undergo inelastic collisions, part of their energy excites atoms, and the atoms emit light. 'Electroluminescence' corresponds to the source's electrical-emission heading and its stated example; there is no claim that ordinary reflection supplies this energy. English has four sentences in one paragraph.

Both retain Sergei Ivanovich Vavilov's identity, 1891 to 1951 lifespan, Soviet identity, 1945 to 1951 Academy presidency, physical optics, photoluminescence, fluorescence polarization, lamp technology and composition analysis. Both retain Cherenkov's 1934 discovery under Vavilov's leadership. Most importantly, both explicitly compare electron speed with light propagation in that medium, never with vacuum c. The surname-only Cherenkov rendering does not invent an expansion of the source initials. Existing people/country declarations are source-bound, but the Academy needs its own institution declaration. English compresses six sentences into one paragraph.

The empty fig block remains exactly in position with id tbl-p0274-01, null label, printed page 264, empty text/source_text and no changes. This PASS concerns text/structure preservation only. No portrait pixels, SVG or modern figure specification were opened or judged.

Both preserve auroral excitation by solar charged particles in the upper atmosphere near the poles and advertising discharge tubes. Replacing literal 'capture by magnetic poles' with the action of Earth's magnetic field clarifies the source explanation without claiming vacuum-superluminal motion or supplying an invented quantitative condition. English's 'textbook's example of electrically excited light emission' matches the Chinese attribution.

Cathodoluminescence remains emission from a solid struck by electrons, with an electron beam supplying the excitation in a cathode-ray-tube television screen. Specifying CRT television avoids presenting this mechanism as an explanation of every modern television. Both use the same mechanism and example.

Both define chemiluminescence through conversion of part of chemical-reaction energy into light. The near-ambient-temperature condition is limited to the cold-light examples discussed in the source, rather than asserted as a universal equality for every reaction. No preliminary heating to incandescence is required; both locales preserve that distinction from thermal emission.

Both retain the summer-night firefly, green-lamp analogy, near-air-temperature emission and examples involving bacteria, insects, deep-sea fish and decaying wood. The disputed back-location wording is explicitly introduced as the textbook's description in both locales; it is not independently asserted as current biology or replaced with a guessed anatomical correction. 'Some' and 'sometimes' avoid blanket claims, without removing an example. English puts the five sentences into one paragraph.

Both locate the original 'not yet practical' chemiluminescent-source claim at the textbook's publication period and explicitly describe it as that period's technology, not a limitation today. Neither invents a publication year, a present-day product example or an independent historical verification. This review accepts the time-bound adaptation of the source claim, not its historical truth as a new SOURCE approval.

Both retain partial reflection and absorption, usual heating by absorbed energy, and photoluminescence as absorption-driven excitation followed by emission. They do not confuse emitted light with reflected light. Neutral holiday-tree ornaments replace the cultural setting while preserving the source's illuminated-decoration example; neither adds a fluorescence lifetime or a phosphorescence condition.

Both preserve the usual, not absolute, longer-emission-wavelength relation and the vessel/organic-dye experiment: violet-filter excitation and yellow-green emission. English 'fluorescein' corresponds to the source dye name. The direction of the wavelength comparison remains longer for the emitted yellow-green light; no wavelength number, concentration or apparatus condition is invented.

Both retain fluorescent-lamp use of photoluminescence, Vavilov's proposed interior coating and excitation by short-wavelength gas-discharge radiation. Country and surname declarations match the source. Using only Vavilov's surname avoids inventing a repair of this block's different printed initial. Both retain the historical 1.5 to 2 consumption range and attribute it to the source's lamps/conditions; neither adds equal light output. Chinese omits the explicit direction of that ratio. English conveys the intended direction, although its comparison construction is less direct than a simple subject-predicate statement, and all four sentences remain in one paragraph.

headings.observation: Chinese chapter/title/printed_title retain exact source headings. English translates them to Chapter 9. Radiation and spectra and Types of radiation and light sources, retaining the printed 102 identifier; section stays null and the source snapshot is unchanged.

historicalIdentities.observation: The historical people, Soviet context, Academy and dates remain in the text. Do not infer or replace uncertain source initials, expand Cherenkov's initials from outside knowledge, or newly certify the source's scientific-history assertions. The missing institution declaration is a metadata completeness defect, not an invitation to change those identities.

paragraphReview.method: Read-only execution of the existing .claude/skills/ld-s10y-lesson/tools/prose_flow.mjs --json on each exact lesson candidate, followed by substantive reading. No HTML, browser, image or visual output was generated or opened.
paragraphReview.zh: Short, coherent two-to-three-sentence paragraphs; no filler requiring revision.
paragraphReview.en: Meaning remains readable, but the charged-particle sentence crosses a paragraph boundary and several paragraphs retain four to six sentences.
paragraphReview.sectionBreaks: Both arrays are empty; no anchors are invented or integer boundaries authored.
paragraphReview.scopeLimit: Paragraph text inspection is not DISPLAY approval and does not certify future native-finalizer output.
